title: Honest Inference for Responder Envelopes in Fixed-Effects Logit Panels
banked_reason: The completed core supplies none of the promised general whole-curve characterization or certificate objects outside its T=2 local chart, and leaves the constructive uniform procedure open.
gap_reasons: The advertised deliverable is a sharp forward-and-reverse Hausdorff-moment characterization of the whole responder-envelope pair (with cross-history gluing, endpoint membership, phase partition, and replayable atomic/SOS certificates), but this node only defines the infinite-dimensional infimum/supremum; the completed core supplies none of those general characterization or certificate objects outside its T=2 local chart.

The recorded topic promises rank/contact-uniform simultaneous inference, whereas this node expressly leaves the required finite regular/contact certificate sets, calibrated selector, error allocation, total overlap rule, and strict whole-curve improvement open; projection alone is a conservative fallback, not that promised constructive procedure.
proof_attempt_summary: The run repaired the T=2 local contact analysis, established the genuine quarter-root elbow and local endpoint limit, and source-matched the FE-logit model and polynomial-target scope. It failed because the field-level core substituted definitions of infinite-dimensional extrema for the promised finite forward/reverse whole-curve characterization and left the constructive rank/contact-uniform procedure as an open question. A faithful rescue would require a new full program implementing continuum phase templates, replayable T=2/T=3 atom/SOS certificates, and a total measurable regular/contact/projection hybrid.
tldr: The note defines the sharp FE-logit responder envelopes for the maintained model and proves the cutoff-margin price of honest inference only on the explicit fixed-nuisance repeated-index \(T=2\) chart. The legal moment geometry, local variance experiment, two-point lower bound, and focal four-cell inversion establish the sharp fixed-sequence scale \(\min\{1,(\sqrt n\Delta^2)^{-1}\}\), with the sole elbow \(\Delta\asymp n^{-1/4}\) and no extra transition at \(v=\Delta B\). The chart is a strict finite-support conditional slice of the Davezies--D'Haultfoeuille--Laage Assumption 1 DGP, while the discontinuous responder indicator is outside their polynomial-target Assumption 3; therefore the lower bound and exact-contact nonadaptation transfer to every ambient responder class containing the chart. The matching upper bound remains chart-specific and uses only four focal cells, so its constant is independent of \(J\) and \(\eta_0\). Whole-curve projection remains the universal fallback, and regular/contact hybridization and higher contacts remain open.
gap: Verified dynamic-panel moment-SDP inference, parametric-rate outer-bound intervals for average effects, and regular whole-function bands do not characterize honest adaptation for a sharp responder endpoint that jumps when a legal atom lies on its cutoff.
fill: Prove the legal-support zero-versus-positive moment regimes and global error inequality, derive the drifting LAN experiment and rational endpoint limit, establish a fixed-sequence two-point honest lower bound, and prove the total inversion's width separately on positive- and zero-regime candidates. Retain fully parameter-dependent projection as fallback and defer any hybrid selector or higher-contact taxonomy until it is well defined.
